source: Agent Contracts: A Formal Framework for Resource-Bounded Autonomous AI Systems
summary: Formal contract C=(I,O,S,R,T,Φ,Ψ) wrapping each agent invocation with input/output specs, resource bounds, temporal limits, and pre/post-conditions; achieves 525x variance reduction and 90% token reduction. Oral presentation at COINE 2026 @ AAMAS 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses the lack of per-stage resource bounds; existing retry issues are reactive, contracts are preventive; maps cleanly onto ProcessRunner + AgentStage config

source: Agent Behavioral Contracts: Formal Specification and Runtime Enforcement for Reliable Autonomous AI Agents
summary: Companion paper to Agent Contracts; focuses on behavioral invariants (what agent must do) vs resource contracts (how much it may consume). Covers drift bounds and recovery mechanisms.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the behavioral side complements HID-147's resource bounds; not a distinct issue but adds depth to the contract model

source: PASTE — Act While Thinking: Pattern-Aware Speculative Tool Execution
summary: Microsoft Research + Shanghai Jiao Tong, March 2026. Pre-executes likely next tool calls while LLM generates, exploiting stable sequential call patterns. 48.5% task time reduction, 1.8x throughput.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge's sequential CLI pipeline has predictable stage→stage transitions (Planning→PlanReview >95%); pre-spawning next subprocess while current runs hides 2-8s startup latency per stage

source: B-PASTE: Beam-Aware Pattern-Guided Speculative Execution for Resource-Constrained LLM Agents
summary: Follow-up to PASTE that extends speculation from single tools to local branch hypotheses (beam search) under strict resource constraints.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — extends HID-148's single-branch pre-spawn to N candidate branches; too complex for initial implementation but worth tracking

source: Self-Healing Agentic Orchestrators for Reliable Tool-Augmented LLM Systems
summary: June 2026 paper formalizing graph-based tool routing with failure taxonomy (hallucinations, exec errors, inconsistent reasoning, tool misuse) and reliability scoring per agent; triggers adaptive replanning when reliability drops.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — provided the reviewer-stall detection and escalation pattern for HID-149; also referenced as foundation for mid-loop model promotion

source: A Self-Healing Framework for Reliable LLM-Based Autonomous Agents (Samsung SDS + Yonsei)
summary: May 2026. First failure taxonomy for LLM multi-agent workflows with runtime reliability scoring and corrective prompting conditioned on failure diagnosis.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — companion inspiration for HID-149 stall detection; reliability scoring maps to per-cycle review quality assessment

source: MAGMA: Multi-Graph Based Agentic Memory Architecture
summary: Jan 2026. Organizes agent memory across semantic, temporal, causal, and entity graphs; policy-guided traversal; top LoCoMo score 0.7; 29.6pt gain on temporal queries.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — already captured in HID-145 (cross-run episodic memory store)

source: BATS: Budget-Aware Test-time Scaling for Tool-Augmented Agents
summary: Google framework; continuous budget-remaining signal enables adaptive tool-call depth; 24.6% vs 12.6% accuracy on BrowseComp vs ReAct baseline.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — already captured across HID-129 (token-budget-aware adaptive granularity) and HID-146 (budget-aware early-stop gate)

source: ZEBRA: Zero-shot Budgeted Resource Allocation for LLM Orchestration
summary: May 2026. Splits a global monetary budget across multi-phase pipeline using nonlinear knapsack via water-filling; 94.4% quality at 50% unconstrained spend.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — already captured in HID-143 (per-stage token budget allocation using zero-shot knapsack controller)

source: BAGEN: Are LLM Agents Budget-Aware?
summary: May 2026. Formalizes budget-awareness as control signal; progressive interval estimation; discovers strong task perf does not correlate with budget-awareness (r=0.35); early-stopping saves 28-64% tokens.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — already captured in HID-146 (budget-aware early-stop gate)

source: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
summary: ICLR 2026. Self-improving system that iteratively modifies its own code via Darwinian evolution archive; SWE-bench from 20% to 50%. Open-source at github.com/jennyzzt/dgm.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — very novel but requires agents that can safely modify their own orchestrator code; significant safety/sandboxing concerns for production system

source: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
summary: May 2026. Source-level adaptation as Turing-complete medium; edits agent harness code (not just prompts/skills); improved grader score from 0.25 to 0.61 in single iteration on OpenClaw.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — more general than prompt-level evolution; source-level changes to orchestrator are possible but require robust sandboxing and human approval gates

source: Karpathy AutoResearch
summary: March 2026, 21k+ stars. Bounded autonomous experiment loop: one editable file, 5-min time-budget per run, single metric. 700 experiments over 2 days, significant val_bpb improvements.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — scope-constrained self-improvement pattern is applicable; but HID-137 (run-outcome-driven stage prompt evolution with A/B variant tracking) covers the core idea sufficiently

source: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
summary: April 2026. Two co-evolving agent populations: Task Agents (solve problems) and Optimizer Agents (refine both populations); dynamic benchmarking; highest absolute peak performance; fully auditable.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — ClaudeCode and Codex as co-evolving populations is a genuinely novel angle; requires second optimizer agent infrastructure; too complex for 1-2 sprint implementation currently

source: DemoEvolve: Overcoming Sparse Feedback in Agentic Harness Evolution with Demonstrations
summary: May 2026. Uses successful trajectory demonstrations to bootstrap harness evolution in low-feedback regimes; combines demo injection with evolutionary search over harness configs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — HID-127 (extend distillation pipeline to extract learnings from blocked/failed runs) and HID-137 cover adjacent territory; demo injection from human clarification events is a distinct angle but overlaps heavily

source: Compiling Agentic Workflows into LLM Weights: Near-Frontier Quality at Two Orders of Magnitude Less Cost
summary: May 2026. Distills procedural workflows into fine-tuned small models (subterranean agents); matches frontier quality at 100x lower cost; reduces context window use and procedure exposure.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — distilling successful AgentForge runs into few-shot injection is a near-term version; but HID-134 (RL-scored cross-run execution trace memory) covers the retrieval angle; fine-tuning is out of scope for the current CLI subprocess architecture

source: A2A Protocol + Linux Foundation AAIF Agent Interoperability
summary: Google A2A (April 2025) + IBM ACP merged into A2A (Aug 2025) + Linux Foundation AAIF permanent home (Dec 2025). Capability cards enable orchestrators to dynamically discover and delegate to agents. Production adoption peaked Q1-Q2 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is an internal orchestrator with hardcoded CLI subprocess agents; A2A would only matter if exposing AgentForge to external agent networks, which is not a current priority

source: awesome-harness-engineering (ai-boost)
summary: Curated harness-level patterns: state machine guardrails by phase, context isolation (67% fewer tokens), loop-detection middleware, deterministic lifecycle hooks (SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook pattern maps to injection points before/after subprocess calls; most patterns already implemented or planned in existing issues

source: awesome-cli-coding-agents (bradAGI)
summary: Only curated list for terminal-native CLI coding agent orchestration; covers Claude Code, Codex, Aider, parallel runners (Claude Squad, cmux), autonomous loop harnesses (claude-flow, gastown). Indexed July 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — closest catalog to AgentForge's architecture; parallel runner patterns worth watching once HID-136 is implemented

source: VoltAgent/awesome-ai-agent-papers 2026
summary: Curated collection of 2026 AI agent research papers covering agent engineering, memory, evaluation, workflows, autonomous systems. Actively maintained.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — useful reference index but not a novel technique; use as a source directory for future research runs
